reviews.text: Not ready for release. Its cool but there's a lot of stuff that make me a bit annoyed with it. You might be wondering what kind of jerk leaves a negative review on a 4 dollar game. I just dont like the game in its current state, even if its cheap, 4 dollars for a game ill never play again still sucks. This game is veeeeeery EA with too many bugs to just go straight to launch so im not sure why they didnt just go EA, going to launch feels a bit disingenuous. Very slow encounters. lots of time is spent just watching enemy turns tick down with nothing to do. A run against 2 bosses took 1.1 hrs, so much of that time was watching the little pocket watch go (-1). The enemy turn doesnt need to happen if nothing happens! Other issues: Memory Leaks, game is sometimes louder than when im playing Space Marine 2.. how or why i dont know. UI bugs everywhere: image variable names loading in descriptions of items Text obscured by z-indexing or obscured by "nothing" you can kinda see text trying to show around parts of the screen. im assuming its the x.5+ when you land the burst effect. weird options to edit your bullet rotation, you can only do it at certain points, not between every fight? Starting a new game and abandoning a run doesnt work. (I didnt play the tutorial and it wouldnt let me get it back when i accidentally clicked the wrong option) Some of the choices i understand help make the game difficult, but other ones are just frustrating and serve no reason than to make the experience worse for the player which is confused with adding difficulty. Does it add difficulty, yes but because it removes something that would objectively make the game better or more fun in a few places. This probably the longest review i ever left for a 3.50 game but just because it charges that much doesnt mean its ok to release a game in this state. some of the best games are cheap and make tons of money because they are good.. not even great.. just good... This isnt event close and its disappointing to see its not EA specially in its current state. I bet it could be ok one day but as a fully launched title i dont think itll ever be good.

[h1][b]牛仔与左轮主题的另类牌组肉鸽[/b][/h1] 《Barrel Roll》是一款西部主题的回合制策略肉鸽游戏，主打构筑玩法，拥有自定义左轮弹夹、子弹队列和技能系统，体验非常独特。 本作中玩家扮演的是一名西部牛仔，目标则是那些被通缉的亡命之徒，战斗间隙可以在酒馆接取任务，或者进行构筑。 游戏最大的特点便是左轮弹夹了，一共可以容纳6发子弹，而这些子弹则由玩家规划，游戏据此打造了拥有诸多效果的弹药，诸如附带燃烧、虚弱、射击时获得增伤等。 游戏以回合制展开，玩家每次可以从射击、技能、装弹等操作中选择一项行动。 弹夹内第一发子弹是固定的，后续则需要按照顺时针转动弹夹来选择子弹，这里并不是严格按照顺序来的，可以选择跳过1-2个子弹。 这套设计富有策略性，第一发固定子弹类似于《杀戮尖塔》中的固有词条，可以保证先手优势，而可跳过的子弹队列则可以应对多种局面。 由于每回合玩家只能行动一次，再加上一对多的战斗模式，游戏也做了相应的平衡，为敌人加上了计时机制，每回合计时都会减少，到零后才会出手。 需要注意的是，如果弹药打光了，需要手动进行装弹，这个操作同样会消耗一回合。 技能会按照一定的系数加强射击伤害，需要专注点才能打出，专注点则会自动增长。 游戏为每个技能都做了简单的小游戏，比如等待聚焦到敌人身上的圆圈出现、快速转动弹夹射击后随机选择一个子弹等。 《Barrel Roll》这套打造左轮的设计非常契合牛仔的设定，玩法简单且有不错的策略性，游戏画面也很有风格，值得一试。 稍显遗憾的是目前本作只支持英文，期待加入汉化了。 [quote]热爱游戏，畅玩游戏，分享游戏，专注鉴赏评测与深度解析 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44110339/]游理游据[/url]，走进游戏世界，品味第九艺术[/quote]

The tl;dr of Barrel Roll [as of 1/27/26]: it just needs more content and some general QoL like animation speed changes or gamespeed adjustments/options; what's there is a pretty solid and fun, while not terribly easy unless the stars align, base that simply has to be fleshed out with MORE to hit its' best. Sure, I've only played 3 hours, and only gotten 1 win in that time, but this game's pretty awesome so far and I hope it gets more content! Music, aesthetics, all of it's great if you ask me. The UI has some minor glitching when it comes to player and enemy shadows blocking intents or descriptions, but is otherwise clean and easy to read and interpret. Once you unlock the second barrel things open up a fair margin too, letting you designate one barrel for different ideas/builds - which is cool. The bosses and overall intent patterns are pretty predictable, though of course you won't always be able to play around them optimally - and that's okay! - with some outright being much easier than others [like Boddie and Clyne]. Strength and debuffs feel great to use, and if you can juice up the shield break for strength bullet it's good enough to carry you a fair ways. Execution+ is pretty phenomenal for ending anything without a shield, even bosses [though I suspect that might get changed, even if I'd prefer it didn't], and the 'adjacent bullets get +4/+7 vs shield as long as this bullet hasn't been fired' adds a lot of value to some key pieces. The Burst minigame is honestly lots of fun when you get in a groove, duel is always satisfying, and gosh I like the Barrel Roll minigame itself - though I think it could stand to either be a bit faster or manipulated in some fashion so it isn't ridiculously easy to get the bullet you want to be fired. In its current state [1/27/26], I'd give this a pretty solid 8/10. Especially at 5 dollars.

Overall recommend this one for the price. Some notes: - At and above the 3rd increased difficulty there are only a few viable strategies, and with the limit to control of your build being entirely random color bullet rewards and shop options save for boss bullets, runs can sometimes be non-starters. - The lack of diversity in general means that you won't play this for more than a few hours probably. - No healing between bounties hurts a fair bit and really hampers cash economy - Why is B barrel locked from the start? It makes the first run feel basically unwinnable and only gives you a disadvantage. All in all dev if you read this, I like the aesthetic and gameplay, it just needs a bit of refinement. I hope you make even cooler games in the future.

As a roguelike and a deckbuilder, Barrel Roll will appeal to those who enjoy a short loop with a clear beginning and end. If you simply enjoy the feeling of putting together your strategy it’s a good way to spend your time. I will say that it appears to be one of the more accessible roguelikes out there — I had things figured out by the second run. Whether that is a positive or negative aspect depends on the player’s preferences. Those who crave a challenge may find it underwhelming or find themselves wanting more after such focused gameplay. This is a game that’s low in scope but high in depth, and will be a fun experience for anyone mechanically-focused who looks forward to a short campaign where you have time to savor every moment. At five dollars and what I’d say is just two hours to a successful run, it’s an easy ask for anyone interested. And if you’re still on the fence, there should be a demo available if you look.
